slides.title: Choose Your Bold Typographic Direction
slides.context: Four bold, high-contrast, internationally-respected graphic design directions. Inspired by your selection of Tokyo Graphic but without kanji elements.

options.label: Swiss International
options.description: Josef Müller-Brockmann style — pure grid, Akzidenz-Grotesk, absolute clarity
options.aside:
The gold standard of graphic design. Objective, universal, timeless.

• Grid-based everything — 1:1.618 ratio, mathematical precision
• Akzidenz-Grotesk or Helvetica — one typeface family only
• Asymmetrical balance, dynamic visual tension
• Objective photography, no decoration
• Limited palette: black, white, one accent (red or blue)
• Flush left, ragged right text alignment

Most respected design tradition in the world. Maximum credibility.

options.label: Vignelli Minimal
options.description: Massimo Vignelli purity — Helvetica, extreme restraint, absolute essentials only
options.aside:
Massimo Vignelli's philosophy: One typeface (Helvetica), a handful of weights, absolute clarity.

• Helvetica only — Light, Regular, Bold, Heavy
• Extreme scale contrast: 72px next to 9px
• Generous whitespace — 60% empty space
• No color except black and one accent
• Everything flush left, no centering
• No decoration, no borders, no shadows

'If you can design one thing, you can design everything.'

Pure, confident, unimpeachable.

options.label: Pentagram Editorial
options.description: Contemporary magazine aesthetic with bold serif/sans contrast
options.aside:
Modern editorial design — think New York Times Magazine, Monocle, The Gentlewoman.

• Bold serif (Tiempos, Freight, Canela) for headlines
• Clean sans (Graphik, Circular) for body
• Dramatic scale contrast with elegant restraint
• Sophisticated palette: warm black, cream, one rich accent
• Generous margins, book-like breathing room
• Subtle sophistication — refinement without flash

Positions you as thoughtful, cultured, and discerning.

options.label: Dutch Modernist
options.description: Wim Crouwel modular grid — total system, mathematical typography
options.aside:
Inspired by Wim Crouwel and the Dutch 'Total Grid' approach.

• Strict modular grid — every element locked to system
• Custom modular typography (like Crouwel's New Alphabet)
• Horizontal/vertical line systems
• Limited but high-contrast palette: black, white, process cyan
• Systematic use of rules and borders
• Almost architectural rigor

'I believe in systems. A system can be very liberating.'

Rigorous, intellectual, utterly distinctive.
